This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 14.10.2014 passed by Addl. MACT, Neemuch in Claim Case No.05/2012 seeking Navin Thru.

The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,30,000/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.75,000/- (lump-sum) Treatment and special diet -Rs.1,50,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.5,000/-
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.2,30,000/-
 =============
3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in awarding lump-sum amount under the head of permanent disability without applying the multiplier method.

The appellant has sustained fracture of talus bone and second metatarsal bone and as per the disability certificate given by the doctor he suffered 35% permanent disability on the lower limb and 14% permanent disability to the whole body.

The Tribunal has not awarded any amount of compensation under the head of future prospects in the matter, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the evidence on record and the permanent disability suffered by him, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.1,27,008/- (i.e. Rs.3000+40% future prospects=4200x14%
(PD)x12x18(multiplier))

Medical Bills -Rs.1,24,000/-
Other conventional heads -Rs.25,000/-
--------------------

6. Thus, the appellant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,76,008/-
as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.2,30,000/-
. Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.46,008/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.46,008/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
